title: Faulty and Logical Comparisons
kicker: American Diploma · Digital SAT · Grammar: Form, Structure and Sense
summary: Compare like with like: that of / those of and possessives, like/unlike openers, than any other, comparative vs superlative and the right partner words — with worked examples and a 10-question practice quiz.

blocks.text: What this question type tests

Comparison questions sit in **Standard English Conventions**, the grammar-and-punctuation domain of the Reading and Writing section (about 26% of the scored questions, usually 11–15 of them). The official skill list does not name comparisons as a separate skill, but they are part of writing sentences whose **form and sense** are correct: a comparison that compares the wrong things is not logical, and the choices often differ only in a possessive (Alexandria / Alexandria's), a pronoun (that / those) or a word form (more / most). Grammar questions usually come after the reading questions in each module.

The stem is the usual one: **"Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?"** Look for comparison signals: **than, as… as, like, unlike, compared with, similar to, different from**, and words ending in **-er / -est** or starting with **more / most**.
Rule 1: Compare like with like

You can only compare things of the **same kind**: a population with a population, a price with a price, a person with a person. The most common mistake compares a **feature** of one thing with the **whole** of another thing. Ask: **What exactly is being compared on the left side? Is the right side the same kind of thing?**

items: ✗ The population of Cairo is larger than **Alexandria**. (population compared with a city)
✓ The population of Cairo is larger than **that of Alexandria**. (that = the population)
✓ Cairo's population is larger than **Alexandria's**. (Alexandria's = Alexandria's population)
✗ The shells of desert snails are thicker than **coastal snails**. (shells compared with snails)
✓ The shells of desert snails are thicker than **those of coastal snails**. (those = the shells)
✗ Mona's handwriting is neater than **her brother**. (handwriting compared with a person)
✓ Mona's handwriting is neater than **her brother's**.

blocks.text: Rule 2: That of, those of, or a possessive
To avoid repeating the noun, English uses three tools. Choose by **number** (singular or plural) and keep the sentence logical.

rows: The cost of rice is higher than **that of** wheat.
The wings of bats are thinner than **those of** birds.
Karim's score was higher than **Mona's**. The lions' cage is larger than **the tigers'**.

items: ✗ The rules of chess are more complex than **that of** checkers. (rules is plural → those of)
✗ Karim's score was higher than **that of Mona's**. (double possessive: use "that of Mona" or "Mona's", never both)
✗ The number of visitors in 2025 was higher than **those** in 2020. (number is singular → that)

blocks.text: **Tip:** replace "that" or "those" with the noun it stands for and read the sentence again: "higher than **the number** in 2020" ✓.
Rule 3: Like, unlike, compared with — at the start of a sentence

An opener such as **Like…, Unlike…, Compared with…, Similar to…** is both a comparison and an introductory modifier. The noun right after the comma must be the **same kind of thing** as the noun in the opener.

items: ✗ **Unlike the earlier model's battery**, the new tablet can run all day. (battery compared with tablet)
✓ **Unlike the earlier model**, the new tablet can run all day. (model vs model)
✗ **Like the ancient Egyptians**, **cats were kept** in many Roman homes. (people compared with cats)
✓ **Like the ancient Egyptians**, **many Romans** kept cats in their homes. (people vs people)
✗ **Compared with last year's exam**, **students** found this year's easier. (exam vs students)
✓ **Compared with last year's exam**, **this year's** was easier.

blocks.text: Rule 4: "Than any other" and "than anyone else"
When you compare one member of a group with the rest of the **same group**, add **other** or **else**. Without it, the sentence says the thing is bigger than itself.

items: ✗ Nour read more books than **any student** in her class. (Nour is a student in her class, so she read more than herself?)
✓ Nour read more books than **any other student** in her class.
✓ Nour read more books than **any student in the other classes**. (She is not in that group, so no "other" is needed.)
✗ Our team scored more than **anyone** in the league. → ✓ more than **any other team** in the league.
✓ The coach worked harder than **anyone else**.

blocks.text: Rule 5: Comparative or superlative?
Use the **comparative** (-er / more / less) for **two** things and the **superlative** (-est / most / least) for **three or more**. Never use both endings at once.

rows: the most practical, the least expensive

items: ✗ Of the two designs, the judges chose **the most practical** one. → ✓ **the more practical** one (two designs)
✗ Of the three proposals, the committee chose **the cheaper** one. → ✓ **the cheapest** one (three proposals)
✗ The new train is **more faster** than the old one. → ✓ **faster** (never more + -er)
✗ This is **the most easiest** route. → ✓ **the easiest** route

blocks.text: Rule 6: Complete the comparison with the right partner word

items: **-er / more … than:** taller **than**, more useful **than** — never "taller **then**" (then = time).
**as … as:** as tall **as**, as much rain **as** — never "as tall **than**".
**different from:** "Her method is different **from** mine" (the safest choice in formal writing).
**the same as / similar to:** "the same **as** last year", "similar **to** a lemon".
**Finish the comparison:** "The new phone is cheaper" is fine only if the text already says cheaper than what; otherwise add "than the old one".

blocks.title: المقارنة لازم تكون بين حاجتين من نفس النوع
items: ماينفعش تقارن «عدد سكان القاهرة» بـ «الإسكندرية» نفسها. قارن عدد سكان بعدد سكان: than that of Alexandria أو than Alexandria's.
لو الحاجة مفرد استخدم that of، ولو جمع استخدم those of.
لو بتقارن حاجة بباقي المجموعة اللي هي منها قول any other. ولحاجتين استخدم -er / more، ولتلاتة أو أكتر -est / most.

blocks.text: The 3-step method for test day

items: **Spot the comparison signal:** than, as… as, like, unlike, compared with, -er/-est, more/most.

**Name the two things being compared.** Read the left side and find its head noun (population, shells, score). Then check that the blank gives the same kind of thing — and the same number (that for singular, those for plural).
**Check the form:** two things → comparative; three or more → superlative; same group → any other; correct partner word (than / as / from).

blocks.text: Worked examples
**Worked example 1: those of**

Snails that live in the dry hills of Sinai must protect themselves from heat and from birds. In a recent survey, researchers measured hundreds of snail shells and found that the shells of snails collected in the hills were thicker than ______ collected near the coast.
**Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?**

items: A) snails
B) those of snails
C) that of snails
D) the snail

blocks.title: Answer: B) those of snails
items: The sentence compares shells. The second side must also be shells: "those of snails" = the shells of snails. "Those" is plural because "shells" is plural (B).
A is wrong: it compares shells with snails (faulty comparison).
C is wrong: "that" is singular, but it replaces the plural "shells" (number error).
D is wrong: it compares shells with a snail, and it is singular (faulty comparison).

blocks.text: **Worked example 2: than any other**
Every year, students at a secondary school in Assiut take part in a reading challenge. This year, Nour read more books than ______ in her class, finishing 64 titles before the summer holiday.
**Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?**

items: A) any student
B) all students
C) every student's
D) any other student

blocks.title: Answer: D) any other student
items: Nour is one of the students in her class, so she must be compared with the **other** students: "any other student" (D).
A is wrong: "any student in her class" includes Nour herself, so she read more than herself (illogical).
B is wrong: "all students" in her class also includes Nour.
C is wrong: the possessive "student's" leaves nothing for it to own; the comparison is between people, not their things.

blocks.text: **Worked example 3: comparative or superlative**

A youth council in Ismailia asked architects to suggest ideas for a new sports center. Of the two designs that reached the final round, the council chose the ______ one, a plan that uses natural light instead of expensive lamps.
**Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?**

items: A) more practical
B) most practical
C) practicaler
D) more practicaler

blocks.title: Answer: A) more practical
items: Only **two** designs are compared, so we need the comparative: "the more practical one" (A). "Practical" is a long adjective, so it takes "more", not -er.
B is wrong: "most" is for three or more things.
C is wrong: "practicaler" is not a word; long adjectives use "more".
D is wrong: never use "more" and -er together.

blocks.text: **Worked example 4: an unlike opener**
The young painter Ahmed Samir trained for years in the studio of a well-known artist who used only soft browns and greys. Unlike the paintings of his teacher, ______ bright, almost electric colors.
**Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?**

items: A) Ahmed likes to use
B) the young artist Ahmed uses
C) Ahmed's paintings are full of
D) Ahmed's style is to use

blocks.title: Answer: C) Ahmed's paintings are full of
items: The opener compares paintings, so the noun after the comma must be paintings: "Ahmed's paintings" (C). Here the possessive is right because the head noun is "paintings".
A is wrong: it compares the teacher's paintings with Ahmed, a person.
B is wrong: same problem — paintings compared with "the young artist".
D is wrong: it compares paintings with a style (head noun "style").

blocks.title: Classic traps
items: **Feature vs whole:** the population of Cairo vs Alexandria, the shells of snails vs snails.
**Wrong number:** that for a plural noun or those for a singular one (the number… those ✗).
**Double possessive:** that of Mona's ✗ — use that of Mona or Mona's.
**Missing "other":** than any student in her class ✗ when she is in the class.
**Two vs three:** the most of two ✗, the -er of three ✗; and never more + -er or most + -est.
**Wrong partner word:** as tall than ✗, taller then ✗.

blocks.title: Fast strategy for test day
items: When choices differ only by that / those / a possessive / no word, it is a comparison question. Find the head noun on the left side first.
Replace that or those with the noun it stands for and read the sentence; if it sounds right, keep it.
Count the things: two → -er/more; three or more → -est/most.
For Like/Unlike openers, use the doer question from the Modifiers lesson: the noun after the comma must match the noun in the opener.
These are quick questions — 30–45 seconds.

blocks.text: Practice

blocks.title: Comparisons — Practice Quiz
blocks.intro: 10 questions in Digital SAT format. Untimed: name the two things being compared before you look at the choices, then read every explanation.

questions.p: The company has released a new tablet for schools. Unlike the earlier model, whose battery lasted only about six hours, ______ can run for an entire school day on a single charge, according to the company.
questions.q: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
c: the battery life of the new tablet
questions.e: "Unlike the earlier model" must compare one model with another model: "the new tablet" (C). A and B compare a model with battery life; D compares a model with users.

questions.p: A survey of public libraries in Giza looked at how teenagers use library services. Researchers found that the number of teenagers borrowing audiobooks in 2025 was nearly double ______ in 2020, when the service was first introduced.
questions.q: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.e: The sentence compares a number with a number. "That" (singular) replaces "the number" (A). B is plural, but "number" is singular; C and D compare a number with teenagers.

questions.p: Botanists at a university in Alexandria grew the same type of lettuce under different colored lights. They found that the leaves of plants grown under red light were wider than ______ grown under blue light.
questions.q: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.e: The sentence compares leaves, which is plural, so the second side needs "those of plants" = the leaves of plants (D). A compares leaves with plants, B uses singular "that" for plural "leaves", and C ("the plant's") is singular and does not match "plants grown".

questions.p: Youssef and Mariam reached the final of the school chess championship. In the end, Youssef's total score was higher than ______, even though she had won more games in the early rounds.
questions.q: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.e: Youssef's score must be compared with Mariam's score: "Mariam's" (B) means Mariam's score. A compares a score with a person, C is a double possessive, and D ("than Mariam had") leaves the comparison incomplete and illogical.

questions.p: A secondary school in Tanta runs a yearly fundraising walk for the local hospital. This year, Class 10B collected more money than ______ in the school, raising over 20,000 pounds in just one weekend.
questions.q: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.e: Class 10B is one of the classes in the school, so it must be compared with the other classes: "any other class" (D). A and B include 10B itself, so it collected more than itself; C uses a possessive that has nothing to own.

questions.p: The city council studied three proposals for a new public park. In the end, it chose the ______ of them, a plan that keeps most of the old trees and needs very little new construction.
questions.q: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.e: There are three proposals, so the superlative is needed: "the least expensive" (B). A is the comparative, used for two things; C is not a correct form; D combines "more" with -er.

questions.p: Two new phone models have almost identical cameras and screens. However, reviewers agree that the Nova has the ______ battery of the two, lasting nearly a full day longer.
questions.q: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.e: "Of the two" means only two things are compared, so the comparative is right: "longer-lasting" (A). B is a superlative (three or more), and C and D combine more/most with -er.

questions.p: Historians have found many signs of how ancient peoples lived with animals. Like the ancient Egyptians, ______ kept cats to protect stored grain from mice.
questions.q: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
c: the homes of many Roman families
questions.e: "Like the ancient Egyptians" compares people with people: "many Roman families" (C). A and B compare people with homes or houses, and D begins with "there", so the Egyptians are compared with nothing.

questions.p: Engineers have built a large solar farm in the desert to supply power to nearby towns. On sunny days, the farm produces nearly as much electricity ______ a medium-sized gas power station.
questions.q: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.e: "As much… as" is the correct pair (A). B ("as much… than") mixes two patterns, C is not used to complete as… as, and D ("then") is a time word.

questions.p: Fishermen say that the sea breeze makes summers in their small coastal town much more comfortable. Thanks to a cold current offshore, the climate of the town is cooler than ______, which lies only thirty kilometers away.
questions.q: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
c: those of the inland city of Damira
that of the inland city of Damira
the inland city of Damira's climates
questions.e: The sentence compares one climate with another, and "climate" is singular, so "that of the inland city" is right (C). A compares a climate with a city, B uses plural "those" for one climate, and D wrongly makes "climates" plural.

blocks.title: Remember
items: Compare like with like: a feature with the same feature, a person with a person.
Use that of (singular), those of (plural) or a possessive — never "that of X's".
Like/Unlike openers: the noun after the comma must be the same kind of thing as the noun in the opener.
Compare one member with the rest of its group using any other / anyone else.
Two things → -er/more; three or more → -est/most; never both at once.
